# A route's markup is built at compile time, so anything it renders has to be a
# literal or an expression over something known per request.

# A window's URL template declares vars -- `/p/{pkg}` puts `pkg` in scope for
# the body. Those are known per request exactly as state is, so markup over one
# renders into a hole rather than being refused.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out_param param.sngl
grep 'HandleFunc' out_param/server.go

# A ternary in markup is html's to render, not the language's. Go has no
# ternary and asks for it to be lowered into a temporary; that rewrote the
# expression into a name the render model could not resolve, and the route was
# refused for markup the JS filling the hole writes verbatim.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out_tern ternary.sngl
grep 'HandleFunc' out_tern/server.go

# The same source under the static backend, which never had the restriction.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out_static ternary.sngl
exists out_static/index.html

# ListLambdas is the language's other withdrawal, and html takes it back for
# the same reason: `.filter`/`.map` in markup are rendered by html, and the Go
# emitter writes an inline lambda directly where it does emit one.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out_lambda lambda.sngl
grep 'HandleFunc' out_lambda/server.go

-- param.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    window #pkg(title="t", href="/p/{pkg}") {
        html.a(href="/p/" + pkg, innerText=pkg)
    }
}

-- ternary.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    var active = true
    window #home(title="t", href="/") {
        html.a(class=active ? "on" : "off", innerText="x")
    }
}

-- lambda.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    var nums list<int> = [1, 2, 3]
    window #home(title="t", href="/") {
        html.span(innerText=string(nums.filter(func(n) => n > 1).length()))
    }
}
